item.title: Staff Post - Wikiwalk Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

This one is largely self-contained, but I do have one simple enough link, ala a link from the mention of the Factory to the GoI Hub. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

SCP-834 is a set of four markers (black, red, yellow and blue.) Each marker bears only a 'The Factory' logo, and no other distinguishing characteristics. The only effect of these markers is that they write permanently on human skin, resulting in tattoo-like markings. Testing has proven the ink sinks below the surface of the skin, and is only removable via laser dermabrasion, or similar tattoo removal procedures. See Addendum.

To this:

SCP-834 is a set of four markers (black, red, yellow and blue.) Each marker bears only a 'The Factory' logo, and no other distinguishing characteristics. The only effect of these markers is that they write permanently on human skin, resulting in tattoo-like markings. Testing has proven the ink sinks below the surface of the skin, and is only removable via laser dermabrasion, or similar tattoo removal procedures. See Addendum.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
(First impressions): This one didn't do a lot for me. It's a little too open-and-shut. I get that a lot of time must have passed between the tattooing and the tattoos becoming literal, so that explains why testing on D-class resulted in the Anomalous classification (D-class get terminated too quickly for the secondary effect to manifest.)

I feel like this will really shine in a Tale when someone from some faction tries to use it creatively. Or people with existing anomalous tattoos come to try and retrieve them.

I wouldn't recommend packing that kind of storytelling into a Recovery Log, though, since that would tip the skip's hand too soon. The one thing I did like about this one is how the Foundation didn't realize the item's true nature until years later when it was too late.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I think there's something no one else mentioned that your post sparked me to comment on… Another reason they were upgraded to Euclid, as well. Perhaps people working with the SCP for too long come under the influence of a slight memetic1 effect that prompts them to use the markers. And I say "slight" because it isn't like it's a crazy impulse in their mind to go steal the markers from containment, but a little suggestion or something in the back of their mind that having an animated tattoo of X "would be awesome!"

That effect isn't mentioned in the article, and I don't believe anyone said anything about it in their comments, but I thought of that almost right away, because it made me think, "Wtf were those researchers thinking? They know better…" kinda like you did at first, before that occurred to me.

Does that maybe help it seem less ridiculous to you now?

Footnotes
1. Did I use memetic properly?

item.content:encoded: The description here is so terse as to be a little bit silly. I mean, I know that there's the whole "it used to be an anomalous object" schtick going on, but it still feels like you could give a bit more. In addition, this whole article feels like it portrays the Foundation's scientists as being little kids who have nothing better to do than draw on themselves with a marker they know is anomalous and that they don't completely understand. Nobody acts like a human being should, and it gave me this real disconnect from the events this article portrayed. This concept can be done without making in it act like a moron.
